question_text: What is meant by chloride shift?

insider_note: Name both ions and say which way each moves. 'Ions are exchanged' is not enough.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question
Breathing and Exchange of Gases · 2 marks

steps.label: What moves
steps.why: Bicarbonate made inside the red cell leaves for the plasma, and something with the same charge has to come in to keep the balance.
common_mistakes: Writing that chloride moves out of the red cell at the tissues. It moves in.
Naming the wrong ions. It is chloride for bicarbonate.
steps.memory_tip: Bicarbonate out, chloride in — at the tissues.
steps.margin_note: Name both ions and both compartments.
lines: Chloride shift is the exchange of chloride
and bicarbonate ions between the red blood
cells and the plasma at the tissues.

steps.label: Why it happens
steps.why: Charge cannot build up on one side of the membrane, so every bicarbonate that leaves is replaced by a chloride.
common_mistakes: Leaving out the reason. The second mark is for the balance of charge.
Saying it happens at the lungs only. It reverses there.
steps.memory_tip: The swap keeps the electrical charge balanced.
steps.margin_note: One line on the reason, one on the reversal.
lines: HCO₃⁻ leaves the red cell and Cl⁻ enters it,

lines.text: At the lungs the shift runs the other way
